newsitem.title: UK: UK's Kenwood urges holders reject proposal.
newsitem.headline: UK's Kenwood urges holders reject proposal.

text.p: Britain's Kenwood Appliances Plc on Monday urged shareholders to reject a move by rebel investors to push the board to consider selling the company.

Kenwood chairman David Nash, speaking at an extraordinary general meeting, reiterated his objection to a proposed resolution that would require the firm to talk with third parties with the aim of soliciting a bid. "Putting up a "For sale' sign over the company would not maximise value," he said in a statement, adding that talks would require the company to disclose sensitive commercial data.
The meeting followed recent moves by rebel shareholders led by Brian Myerson and Julian Treger and their UK Active Value group aimed at selling the company.
Last week, Pifco Holdings Plc said that Kenwood had rejected two of its recent proposals which called for a merger of the two companies.
Kenwood's Dash confirmed that the company was approached by Pifco, but added that it never received a formal bid.
